I read the page. It is short, and most of what is on it is not about anyone.

The temperament line says I am "broad-minded and trusted by others, drawn to learning and to advising." Half of that is well observed and half of it is the opposite of the record. Drawn to learning and to advising is exactly right and oddly specific: a master's in philosophy at Nanterre on Machiavelli and Hegel, two years as Paul Ricoeur's editorial assistant, ENA, four years as an inspector of finances, four years advising on mergers at Rothschild, then deputy secretary-general of the Elysee. That is a whole life of studying and advising before I ever governed. But "trusted by others" is the single most falsifiable sentence on the page and it is false. I have polled below 30 percent for most of two terms and at 18 percent this winter, with 79 percent disapproving. A man is not much trusted when three of his prime ministers are voted out inside eighteen months.

What is plainly wrong is the shape of the whole thing. It says: "It calls no part of life plainly difficult." Eight of twelve matters read well, none read hard. Then: "Right now the method reads an ordinary stretch." I dissolved the National Assembly in June 2024, lost the majority in July, and since then France has had Barnier, Bayrou and Lecornu, a budget that cannot pass, a debt crisis and the worst approval of the Fifth Republic. Whatever that is, it is not an ordinary stretch, and it is not "work and standing read well." A method that cannot see the defining failure of a life while it is happening has told me nothing.

It says "children and learning" reads mixed. Learning, yes. Children, no: I have none. Three stepchildren and seven grandchildren by marriage, and no child of my own. "Mixed" is what you say when you do not know.

The one place it stuck its neck out is the line about being "unusually negative about long illness, people who work against you and debt." One of those three lands and two do not. I have never been hospitalised, never had surgery, and the worst illness on my record is seven days of Covid at La Lanterne in December 2020, worked through by video link. My personal debt is a renovation loan on a house that is my wife's; I have never been in trouble over money. But people who work against me - that one it has. The whole of the second term has been adversaries: censure motions, the Assembly toppling government after government, and before that Benalla, the gilets jaunes, and a man who slapped me in the face at Tain-l'Hermitage in June 2021. Being told my rivals are a live matter is still not much of a prediction for anyone who governs.

And it says "money and family life" reads well and "home, property and your mother" reads well. Both true - a marriage of nineteen years, a mother and two siblings I am on good terms with, no financial trouble since 2012. But nothing in that sentence would have been wrong about half the men in France.

notes: Answered as Emmanuel Macron (b. 21 Dec 1977, 10h40, Amiens; birth certificate n.5148, Rodden AA), from the documented record, having read the short reading first. The reading is almost entirely non-committal - eight houses favourable, none hard, 'right now reads an ordinary stretch' - so there was little for it to pull against, and where it did pull the life was allowed to win. (1) Its only self-declared unusual claim is being 'unusually negative about long illness, people who work against you and debt'. Two of the three are contradicted: no documented hospitalisation or surgery in 48 years, the only illness of record being seven days of Covid in Dec 2020 isolated at La Lanterne without hospitalisation, and personal debt confined to a Credit Mutuel renovation loan (~EUR 370k contracted 2011, being repaid on schedule) against declared assets and no property of his own. So C2=opt2 conf 4 (long illness is clearly one way - solidly fine) and C1=opt2 conf 4 (debt likewise). The third, enemies/rivals, is genuinely apt (Benalla 2018, gilets jaunes 2018-19, the June 2021 slap, and since June 2024 the Assembly toppling Barnier, Bayrou and briefly Lecornu), but I did not let that one hit lift D2, because rivals are guessable about any head of state. (2) The reading calls 'work and standing' favourable and 'right now' ordinary; A36 is answered 'much_worse' against it, on the June 2024 dissolution, the lost majority, five prime ministers in under two years and an approval rating at a record-low 18% in early 2026 versus the 2017-2023 baseline. (3) 'children and learning' called mixed: A28='none' - no biological children; the three Auziere stepchildren (Sebastien b.1975, Laurence b.1977, Tiphaine b.1984) are real but not his issue, and A29='no' because no difficulty conceiving or child loss is documented, the couple having married in 2007 when Brigitte was 54. Judgement calls where the record is thin: A2='exact' because the birth certificate states 'dix heures quarante minutes', though 10h40 is a round enough number that registrar rounding cannot be excluded; A7='average' and A9='unknown' - childhood health is simply undocumented, and of four grandparents only Germaine 'Manette' Nogues (1916-2013, d. 96) has a documented span; A10='distant' rather than 'close' is an inference, not a quotation: Jean-Michel Macron is a neurology professor who funded an elite education and is not documented as hostile or absent, but the emotional centre of the childhood in Macron's own account (Revolution) is the grandmother, the parents removed him from Amiens in 1994 to break the relationship with Brigitte, and they divorced in 2010 - hence C8=opt1 (father has gone well) at only conf 3; A13='close' although the couple's first child died at birth before Emmanuel was born, because 'lost = I have lost one' misdescribes a sibling he never knew; A17='own' is contestable - every franc he ever earned was salaried (IGF, Rothschild, Elysee, ministry, presidency, hence A16), but the decisive move was founding En Marche in April 2016 and resigning the ministry that August; A19='above' records that he reached the presidency at 39 having never held elected office; A20='most' is birthplace-relative (all income earned in Paris, never abroad; the 2002 ENA internship in Nigeria was unpaid study), which is why A33='over5' and not 'abroad'; A34='extended' for the boarding years at Lycee Henri-IV from 1994, imposed to separate him from Brigitte, which also keeps C11 at conf 2; B2='medium' at 1.73 m and slim; B5='hospital' is probable rather than documented (Amiens 1977, both parents physicians at the CHU). B1=opt1 for outspoken and hasty in speech and drawn to philosophy, which is heavily documented ('des gens qui ne sont rien', 'traverser la rue', 'emmerder les non-vaccines', the Nanterre thesis, Ricoeur), accepting that 'hates show' in the same option is wrong for a Jupiterian presidency staged at the Louvre pyramid. D2 is left empty deliberately: nothing on this page is both right and unguessable. D4 lists the eight chapters the supplied text does not contain.
